title: The Opera Game
summary: Paris, 1858: Paul Morphy beats two noblemen in a box at the opera, with the most famous queen sacrifice in chess.

steps.title: Paris, 1858
steps.text: Paul Morphy is twenty-one, from New Orleans, and beating everyone in Europe. One evening at the Paris opera, the Duke of Brunswick and Count Isouard invite him to their box, and challenge him mid-performance. Morphy plays the game of his life while the opera plays on. Seventeen moves. Press play.
steps.narration: Paris, 1858. At the opera, two noblemen challenge the twenty-one-year-old Paul Morphy during the performance. Seventeen moves later, chess history is made. Press play.

steps.title: Morphy – Duke Karl & Count Isouard, Paris 1858
steps.text: Morphy's two opponents consult on every move, and it doesn't help. This game is still the perfect lesson in fast development: every Morphy piece comes out with a threat.
steps.narration: Two opponents, consulting on every move. It does not help. Watch the perfect lesson in development.

notes.text: 3.d4! Morphy opens the center immediately. Development is everything to him.
6.Bc4: every piece comes out, and each one comes out with a threat.
7.Qb3! Double attack on b7 and f7. The consultants are already under pressure.
9.Bg5: the knight is pinned to the queen. The pressure never stops for a single move.
10.Nxb5! Morphy sacrifices a knight to tear open the lines toward the king.
12.O-O-O: the king is safe AND the rook lands on the open file. Two goals in one move.
13.Rxd7! The rook sacrifice. Black's defenders get dragged off their squares one by one.
15.Bxd7+ Nxd7, and now the back rank has almost no defenders left.
16.Qb8+!! The queen sacrifice: the knight is forced to take…
17.Rd8# Checkmate! Perhaps the most famous finish in all of chess: played between acts at the opera.

steps.title: Morphy's finish
steps.prompt: Black's king and rook are lined up on the back rank. Find Morphy's famous mate in two.
steps.hint: The queen can go where she can be taken: if taking her opens the d-file.
steps.success: Qb8+!! Nxb8 Rd8#: the Opera Game's immortal finish. You played it like Morphy.
steps.narration: Now you are at the opera. Mate in two: find Morphy's finish.

steps.title: The big lesson
steps.question: Players have studied the Opera Game for over 160 years. What is its big lesson?

options.text: Develop every piece quickly and open lines toward the king
options.why: Exactly. Morphy's pieces all joined the attack while Black's rook and bishop never moved.

options.text: Keep the queen at home until the endgame
options.why: Morphy's queen led the attack, and even sacrificed herself to finish it.
Morphy gave material away. Time and open lines were worth more to him than pieces.

steps.narration: One question to finish: what is the lesson of this game?
